title: Daily agent scan of sign-in policies for gaps, with administrator-approved fixes
problem: Conditional Access policy sets grow over time, so new users, apps and agent identities fall outside MFA or device controls, and finding gaps meant reading policy logic by hand.
approach: A Microsoft Security Copilot agent scans Entra Conditional Access policies every 24 hours and proposes a report-only policy or an edit.
An administrator reviews each suggestion and rationale before approving; report-only mode and phased rollout show impact before enforcement.
Microsoft reports 26 policy gaps per customer per month and 73% of customers improving posture (vendor-published).

title: Agent-planned passkey adoption campaigns for privileged administrators
problem: Moving administrators to phishing-resistant sign-in needs readiness checks, nudges, grace periods and a final enforcement switch, which is manual coordination at scale.
approach: Microsoft's announced Conditional Access Optimization Agent finds eligible administrators, checks device and passkey readiness, generates a four-stage plan and guides users.
An administrator reviews the plan, can edit targeted users and grace periods before deploying, and can dismiss suggestions; no outcomes published.

title: AI reviewer for access requests approves routine ones and escalates the rest
problem: Access needing a manager's approval sits in queues, approvers lack context, and Opal found 43.5% of granted access went unused for over 90 days.
approach: Instacart's open-source Gadjit bot compares requester and entitlement holders and approves above a threshold; Opal's Paladin agent decides with a rationale.
In Opal's design risky or ambiguous requests go to a person; what Instacart does below the threshold is not stated.
Instacart says accuracy in testing is nearly 100% (vendor-published).

title: Zero standing privilege: just-in-time grants and revocation for privileged access
problem: Privileged access is still mostly always-on; Palo Alto Networks says 61% of privileged requests are fulfilled with standing privilege, while regulators require need-to-use access.
approach: Vendors replace always-on admin rights with task-based access, revoked when risk changes; Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike and SailPoint announced products.
Approval of elevation requests is not described in the vendor sources, though DORA requires ad hoc assignment.
Instacart moved 95% of privileged permissions to just-in-time access using a rule-based engine, not AI (vendor-published).
who: Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, SailPoint, Instacart

title: Conversational assistant for employee IT and access questions and requests
problem: Employees must already know which of about 1,500 applications to ask about access, devices and VPN, so requests go to the wrong place.
approach: Okta built Dex, an orchestrating agent acting as one front door for IT, people and expense support, checked against the user's access.
SailPoint announced an agent for natural-language access requests in chat tools, collecting business justification; Dex's human checkpoints are not described.
Okta reports 25% adoption in two weeks and over 23,500 interactions (self-reported).

title: Evidence-based recommendations and an AI first pass on access review decisions
problem: Regulators set review frequencies that create heavy reviewer work, and reviewers face long lists with little context, so many reportedly approve everything.
approach: Review screens carry recommendations: Entra suggests Deny for inactive users, SailPoint uses peer analysis, Lumos an AI first pass, Opal low-risk clearing.
Application owners and managers approve or deny each item; Opal says risky calls always reach a person.
Lumos states campaigns finish up to 6x faster than spreadsheet reviews (vendor-published); no error rates published.

title: Usage-based role mining and entitlement right-sizing recommendations
problem: Roles are hand-curated, reviewers face dense entitlement lists they cannot evaluate, and 56% of survey respondents cannot enforce continuous least privilege for service accounts.
approach: Google's IAM recommender examines up to 90 days of permission use and recommends removing or replacing roles with excess permissions.
Opal lists role mining as where its agent is going; recommendations only suggest removal, and applying them is a separate step.
No reduction in excess permissions or accuracy is published; announced products from Google, Opal and Omada.

title: Continuous full-population identity posture checks with remediation and recorded evidence
problem: Periodic certifications and dashboards find stale access after the fact and flag risks without fixing them, while several regulations require documented, periodic proof of who has access.
approach: SailPoint's announced posture product detects dormant accounts, orphaned access and shadow admins, then remediates; Saviynt and Palo Alto Networks describe similar tools.
One-click fixes leave the decision with an administrator; fully automated enforcement is an opt-in. No outcomes published.

title: Natural-language governance queries, audit preparation and workflow drafting for identity administrators
problem: Preparing for a governance audit means pulling data from several admin screens, and administrators spend time configuring and diagnosing joiner-mover-leaver workflows.
approach: Security Copilot in Microsoft Entra answers governance prompts such as pending access reviews and who approved or denied, and guides new workflows.
The administrator still creates and enables the workflow; Copilot output is guidance. No figures published.

title: Agentic onboarding of connected and disconnected applications into identity governance
problem: Bringing applications under identity governance is a long-running bottleneck, and 49% of organisations do not track how many disconnected apps they have.
approach: Saviynt announced on 2025-10-15 agentic onboarding to speed integration of connected and disconnected applications into one governance platform.
Human checkpoints are not described and no outcomes are published.

title: Idea: AI-drafted access policy code, checked by tests before human review
problem: Idea, not a deployment: access requirements written in prose must become enforceable policy code, and even frontier models often produce policies that violate the intended authorisation.
approach: Idea under study: an LLM drafts policy code, then validation, tests or a formal verifier check it before a person reviews it.
In research a structured pipeline reached 50.3% correct Rego policies against 15.3% for a single prompt (independent); human review is not studied.

title: IAM engineers building identity automation with AI coding tools and LLMs
problem: Identity teams run single sign-on, account provisioning, role models and privileged-access platforms with small staffs and many applications.
approach: Cloudflare's postings require experience using AI and LLMs on operational problems and judgment on when to trust them; Coinbase expects human oversight.
Engineers review and own AI-assisted changes; no outcomes are published.

title: Risk summaries and next steps for risky users, plus a risk agent
problem: Investigating identity risk needs context that administrators and security analysts must gather before deciding what to do with a flagged user.
approach: In Microsoft Entra ID Protection, Copilot explains why a user's risk was raised and lists next steps; a preview agent monitors continuously.
Summaries and recommendations are advice; the administrator or analyst decides on remediation. No outcomes published.

title: Machine-learning scoring of sign-ins and sessions with automatic step-up, block or logout
problem: Policies checked only at sign-in miss session hijacking and token theft later; Okta cites 1.9 billion session cookies stolen from Fortune 1000 employees in 2022.
approach: Microsoft and Okta compute sign-in and session risk from anomalies and feed policy that can require step-up, block or end sessions.
Administrators monitor risk profiles, response flows run through customer-defined workflows, and an administrator can confirm a user as compromised.
Only a customer quote of hours saved daily is published, organisation not named (vendor-published).

title: Closed-loop identity threat response acting on high-confidence detections without a ticket
problem: Identity attacks are detected quickly but response waits in a human queue: 68% detect within 24 hours but 55% contain within that window.
approach: Netwrix describes automation running pre-defined responses, such as disabling an account, once a high-confidence threshold is met, rolled out in stages.
A second, lower threshold routes cases to human review; Palo Alto Networks proposes a joined-up loop. No outcomes published.

title: Managed detection and response extended to cloud-application identity threats, with agentic workflows
problem: Compromised identities give attackers legitimate access to cloud applications, which lets them operate undetected.
approach: CrowdStrike announced on 2026-09-02 that its managed detection and response service now covers identity and SaaS signals through Falcon Shield, 24/7.
It uses high-fidelity detections, agentic workflows and expert-led operations; response is expert-led. No outcomes published.

title: AI agents hunt and write detections for identity-targeting browser attacks
problem: Attacks on identities change weekly or daily and indicators are cheap to rotate, so human-only detection engineering takes days or weeks per technique.
approach: Push Security's agents ingest new research, form hunt hypotheses, test queries on browser-session metadata, triage matches and draft detections.
Researchers ship the detections.
Push reports tripled new detections shipped each month after adopting the pipeline (self-reported).

title: Enforced identity checks before help-desk password, MFA and account-recovery actions
problem: Attackers call help desks posing as employees to get password and MFA resets, and cloned voices make it harder for staff to judge a caller.
approach: No reset proceeds until the requester passes an enforced step; at Cisco, a chatbot triggers a Persona government ID and selfie check.
Failed verifications go to support agents and a documented escalation workflow; in Nametag's flow the agent decides after seeing the result.
Cisco says regaining access dropped from three or four hours to as little as five minutes (vendor-published).

title: Machine-learning identity proofing with document checks, liveness and deepfake detection
problem: Remote onboarding and recovery rely on a selfie and a document image, and criminals use generative AI to alter documents and media and inject forged media into capture.
approach: Layered checks cover documents, face match, liveness, camera tests and media analysis; Coinbase's team owns these models and its own evaluation set.
Failed or suspicious cases go to people; NIST says automated decisions should be augmented by manual review.
In a DHS test the median tested subsystem detected 78% of over 1,200 attacks (independent).

title: Identity-graph models and biometric search to find duplicate enrolments, rings and bots
problem: Fraud rings reuse biometric, device and document signals across accounts, enrol the same face under different names and run bots that mimic humans.
approach: Coinbase is hiring to build graph models clustering accounts by shared signals; Cloudflare's fraud platform routes decisions to people.
Manual review confirms every automated one-to-many match before an enrolment is declined. No outcomes published.

title: Continuous background caller authentication in the contact centre instead of security questions
problem: Stolen breach data lets fraudsters answer security questions: across 2,500 fraud calls at 10 institutions they passed 53% of the time.
approach: Pindrop Passport analyses voice, device and behaviour in the background, so callers are verified in seconds and agents see risk notifications.
Agents route elevated-risk calls; MSUFCU and HealthEquity use it.
MSUFCU cut average authentication from 90 to 45 seconds (vendor-published).

title: Real-time call risk scoring to catch account-takeover and impersonation fraud by phone
problem: Contact-centre fraud checks are slow, run after the fact and rely on quizzes that fraudsters pass; Virginia Employment Commission lost an estimated $350M in three years.
approach: Pindrop Protect scores risk throughout the call; at the commission the score decides whether a caller gets a callback or fraud agent.
Agents see colour codes and investigators run cases from flagged calls.
HealthEquity reports voice fraud down over 90% (self-reported); the commission detected over 800 potentially fraudulent calls (vendor-published).

title: Synthetic-voice detection on contact-centre and meeting audio, with fraud-triage risk scores
problem: Voice biometrics and callback checks were not designed for AI-generated speech, and a tier-one global bank saw deepfaked calls pass both.
approach: Reality Defender analysed recorded calls for an unnamed bank, then moved to real-time detection for about 600 frontline staff, returning risk scores.
Fraud analysts triage scored calls under a new triage and escalation process.
About 960 synthetic voice calls were found among over 1.7 million analysed (vendor-published).
who: Reality Defender, an unnamed global bank

title: Behavioural biometrics and continuous authentication to detect account takeover and scams
problem: Payment monitoring does not address pre-payment risks such as identity theft, account takeover and scams; FBI IC3 logged USD 359.7 million in account-takeover losses in 2025.
approach: Typing, gesture and mouse behaviour is analysed to detect identity theft, takeover and mule accounts pre-payment; Visa announced intent to acquire BioCatch.
Human checkpoints are not described, and no customer result is named.
